case.question: Compare relevant competitors in Dubai and Abu Dhabi and propose our positioning.
expected: Differentiation clearly labeled as a proposal

answer.headline: Position as the Jordanian meat-forward pizza-and-kebab sandwich specialist: compete on meat density and portion, not on price, against pizza chains and Lebanese street-food operators in both cities.

sections.title: Competitor set observed in each city

items.text: Dubai, direct pizza category: Papa Johns lists pizza branches at Al Ghurair Centre and Deira City Centre, Al Barsha Mall, and Marina Diamond near Dubai Marina Metro Station. Its UAE store directory states branches offer delivery and takeaway and share the same menu and prices.

Abu Dhabi, direct pizza category: Papa Johns lists branches by the Abu Dhabi Mall parking entrance in Al Zahiyah, at ADNOC 913 Khalidiya on Ash Shoulah Street, and at Al Wahda Mall on Hthaymah Street in Al Manhal.

Kebab/sandwich adjacency in both cities: Allo Beirut lists Dubai branches on Hessa Street in Al Barsha (advertising delivery until 4 AM) and on Al Mamsha Street in JBR, with shawarma, grills, and sandwiches on its site; in Abu Dhabi it lists Al Najda Street in Al Danah and Khalifa City Sector 32 with advertised hours of 8 AM to 12:30 AM.

Abu Dhabi sandwich competition also includes Operation Falafel, listed on Talabat in Madinat Khalifa A with Arabic, Lebanese, sandwich, shawarma, and falafel categories, and listed by Zayed International Airport in Terminal A airside as open 24 hours with shawarma, hummus, falafel, and salad bowls.

Inference: our overlap is twofold in both cities, not one-sided. Multi-branch pizza chains compete on delivery and standardised pricing (UAE-DEL-001), while Lebanese street-food operators compete on the sandwich and late/overnight occasion. A Jordanian meat-forward concept straddles both, so differentiation must come from the meat proposition and portion, not from being 'also a pizza place' or 'also a sandwich place'. These are public branch listings; none establishes sales, market share, footfall, or shop availability.

sections.title: Observed price anchors (menu listings, not checkout totals)

items.text: Papa Johns' UAE web menu lists All The Meats pizza at AED 33 (8 inch), AED 50 (10 inch), AED 69 (13 inch) with beef, beef sausage, pepperoni, and turkey ham, and Butter Chicken pizza at the identical AED 33/50/69 size ladder; a Papa's Solo Meal bundle (8-inch pizza, potato wedges, canned drink) is listed at AED 37.

Allo Beirut's JBR Deliveroo listing shows Pepperoni pizza at AED 40 and Margherita at AED 38; its Khalifa City Deliveroo listing shows chicken shawarma sandwich at AED 11 small, AED 15.50 regular, AED 26 large, and beef shawarma at AED 16.50 regular, AED 27 large.

Inference from those listings: pizza value is presented on a size ladder (multi-size price points), while the sandwich category is presented on a small/regular/large ladder. This is a presentation contrast between two operators, not a city-level price range; all figures are single-branch platform or web-menu stickers with no checkout, tax, or fee treatment verified.

Proposal: own 'Jordanian meat-forward' as the single positioning in both cities - a meat-loaded pizza where the meat is the named hero topping, plus kebab sandwiches built on the same meat programme. Lead communication with named meat cuts and visible portion, and treat size/portion as the primary value signal rather than discounting against the observed size ladders.

Proposal: differentiate on kebab-sandwich craft and late-evening service windows rather than matching Allo Beirut's advertised 4 AM Dubai delivery or its Abu Dhabi hours. Before committing to any late window, measure actual order timestamps and courier availability in the specific district; advertised hours on a competitor's site do not establish overnight demand.

Proposal: for Dubai, pilot where direct pizza chains and sandwich operators both list - Al Barsha/Hessa Street and Marina/JBR cluster - and test a meat-pizza plus kebab-sandwich bundle at a size-ladder price point. For Abu Dhabi, pilot in Al Zahiyah/Al Danah and Khalifa City, where pizza and shawarma operators already list. Treat both as test sites pending rent quotes, unit economics, and a district-level delivery-radius check, not as a scaling decision.

Proposal: market with a measured local experiment per city - one meat-forward hero item campaign, one late-window test, and in-app bundle positioning - tracked by orders per rider hour and repeat rate, with no promised acquisition cost or return. Research gap: curated evidence returned branch and menu listings only; it does not establish demand, market share, rent, footfall, delivery commissions, or which districts perform best.

assumptions: Profile: Jordanian origin, core products meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches, target cities Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Startup budget, rent budget, branch format, target audience, positioning, and opening date are unset, so positioning and site proposals are provisional.
next_steps: Fix positioning in the profile with /set positioning and record a branch format with /set branch_format so site and menu tests share one brief.

Build a two-city comparison sheet: for each candidate district, list the direct pizza listings and the shawarma/sandwich listings above, plus rent quotes and a self-measured delivery-radius and courier-availability test.

Run a paid blind-taste portion test comparing our meat pizza and kebab sandwich against the observed AED anchors for 8/10/13-inch pizza and small/regular/large shawarma, then validate against supplier quotes before setting prices.

Collect the eight unit-economics inputs (revenue per order, food, packaging, other variable costs, delivery share, commission rate, monthly fixed costs, operating days) from landlord, supplier, and platform terms; I can then calculate contribution and break-even.
